'''Maximilian Kleber''' (born 29 January 1992) is a German professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He spent the first seven years of his career playing in Germany and Spain. In 2017, he joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]], with whom he would play until being traded to the Lakers in 2025.

==Early life==
Kleber played in the youth ranks of TG Veitshöchheim, SC Heuchelhof and TG Würzburg.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 July 2014 |title=Maximilian Kleber wechselt nach Spanien |language=de-DE |work=mainpost.de |url=http://www.mainpost.de/sport/wuerzburg/Basketball-Maximilian-Kleber-wechselt-nach-Spanien;art786,8211903 |access-date=13 July 2017 |archive-date=29 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829203719/https://www.mainpost.de/sport/wuerzburg/Basketball-Maximilian-Kleber-wechselt-nach-Spanien;art786,8211903 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Würzburg (2011–2014)===
Kleber made his professional debut in Germany's top-flight [[Basketball Bundesliga]] during the 2011–12 season, representing the [[s.Oliver Baskets]], a team based in his hometown [[Würzburg]]. In his first year, he was a role player on the team with an average of 7 minutes a game. In his second season, he grew to become an important player on the team, that averaged 9.9 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maximilian Kleber Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Maximilian-Kleber/Summary/27060 |accessdate=10 November 2024 |publisher=Basketball.realgm.com}}</ref> In 2012, he declared for the [[NBA draft]] before removing his name from the list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maximilian Kleber 2012 Underclassmen |url=https://www.thedraftreview.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=7723 |access-date=10 November 2024 |website=thedraftreview.com}}</ref> He became auto-eligible for the [[2014 NBA draft|NBA draft in 2014]], but was not picked by any team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Maximilian-Kleber/Summary/27060|title=Maximilian Kleber Player Profile, Bayern Munich, News, Rumors, International Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Awards – RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com|access-date=13 July 2017}}</ref>

===Obradoiro (2014–2015)===
In the 2014 off-season, he signed a two-year deal with Spanish club [[Obradoiro CAB]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=2 July 2014 |title=Obradoiro announces Maxi Kleber |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/125343/obradoiro-announces-maxi-kleber.html |accessdate=10 November 2024 |publisher=archive.sportando.basketball}}</ref> In the [[2014–15 ACB season]], he was named [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of round 25 after scoring 36 points against [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=111798|title=Maxi Kleber, Jugador de la Jornada 25|trans-title=Maxi Kleber, Player of the Round 25|publisher=ACB.com|date=22 March 2015|accessdate=15 April 2015|language=Spanish|archive-date=25 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325162237/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=111798|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kleber made 33 appearances in the league that year, averaging 11.5 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historial estadístico – Kleber, Maxi |url=http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=1KZ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006195248/http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=1KZ |archive-date=6 October 2018 |access-date=13 July 2017 |website=acb.com |language=es-ES}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich (2015–2017)===
On 1 July 2015, Kleber returned to Germany and signed a two-year deal with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Barkas |first=Aris |date=1 July 2015 |title=Bayern Munich signs Maximilian Kleber to a two-year contract |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/transfers/106919/maxi-kleber-to-bayern-munich/ |accessdate=10 November 2024 |work=eurohoops.net}}</ref> In 2015–16, he played 24 Bundesliga games for Bayern, including 17 starts, averaging 8.0 points and 4.9 boards per game. He appeared in 37 games (37 starts) during the 2016–17 Bundesliga season, supplying averages of 9.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.

===Dallas Mavericks (2017–2025)===
On 13 July 2017, Kleber signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wermuth |first=Adam |date=13 July 2017 |title=Mavericks Sign Forward Maxi Kleber |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-forward-maxi-kleber/ |accessdate=13 July 2017 |website=mavs.com}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on 21 October 2017 against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974783|title=James Harden leads Rockets past Mavericks, 107–91|publisher=ESPN|date=22 October 2017|access-date=22 October 2017}}</ref> Kleber moved from end of bench piece to key rotation player in his first few years, increasing his points, rebounds, assists and blocks per game numbers in each of his first three seasons. He was re-signed by the Mavericks on 10 July 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-re-sign-forward-maxi-kleber/|title=Mavs re-sign forward Maxi Kleber|publisher=mavs.com|date=10 July 2019|accessdate=10 July 2019}}</ref>

On 21 February 2020, Kleber scored a career-high 26 points against the [[Orlando Magic]] in a 122–106 victory. In the 2019–20 season, Kleber posted a career high 9.1 points per game. He led the league in games played with 74 games and finished 19th in the league in blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 October 2021 |title=Maxi Kleber NBA Statistics |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/klebima01.html |accessdate=23 October 2021 |website=basketball-reference.com}}</ref> Kleber played in his first playoffs that year against the second seed [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Kleber was tasked with guarding [[Kawhi Leonard]] for most of the series. Kleber struggled shooting the ball in the series, averaging 6.7 points per game and making just 5 of his 26 three-point attempts across the six-game series.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 October 2021 |title=Season Recap |url=https://mffls.com/blog/2020/8/30/sll9ed6zm8wh142yw7a54wzc4s4q3d-luka-doncic-kawhi-leonard-kristaps-porzingis-dallas-mavericks-game-6 |accessdate=23 October 2021 |website=mffls.com }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

Kleber began the 2020–21 season strong, averaging 7.4 points per game and shooting 47.2% from three-point range in his first 9 games. Kleber would go on to miss the next 10 games however, as he recovered from [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Afseth |first=Grant |date=23 October 2021 |title=Dallas Mavs' Maxi Kleber opens up on COVID |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-maxi-kleber-covid-luka-doncic-injury |accessdate=23 October 2021 |website=si.com}}</ref> Kleber would return to action 2 February 2021 against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He logged 17 minutes of game play, grabbing 6 rebounds and scoring 2 points. Kleber and the Mavericks would go on to lose to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the first round of the playoffs in 7 games.

On 18 April 2022, during game 2 of the first round of the playoffs, Kleber scored 25 points and hit eight 3-pointers in a 110–104 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brunson scores 41, Mavs make 22 3s in Game 2 win vs Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401430232 |access-date=19 April 2022 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> In the 2022 off-season, he signed a four-year contract extension with the Mavericks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Dwain |date=8 September 2022 |title=Mavs sign Maxi Kleber to contract extension |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavsextendkleber/ |access-date=8 September 2022 |website=mavs.com}}</ref>

On 17 March 2023, Kleber made a buzzer-beating, game-winning three-pointer in a 111–110 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavs-news-lakers-stunned-buzzer-maxi-kleber-dagger-three-over-anthony-davis|title=Lakers stunned at the buzzer by Maxi Kleber dagger three over Anthony Davis|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=R.P.|date=17 March 2023|access-date=17 March 2023}}</ref> Kleber helped Dallas reach the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=17 June 2024|date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2025–2026)===
{{See also|Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade}}
On 2 February 2025, Kleber was traded, alongside [[Luka Dončić]] and [[Markieff Morris]], to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Max Christie]], [[Anthony Davis]] and a 2029 first-round pick. The Lakers also traded [[Jalen Hood-Schifino]] and a 2025 second round pick to the [[Utah Jazz]], who also acquired a 2025 second-round pick from the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Luka Dončić, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris from Dallas Mavericks|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-acquire-doncic-kleber-morris-from-mavericks-020225|website=NBA.com|date=2 February 2025|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

On April 30, 2025, during the first round of the playoffs, Kleber made his debut for the Lakers. He scored two points in a 103–96 loss against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], eliminating the Lakers from the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 1, 2025 |title=Rudy Gobert dominates small-ball Lakers and the Timberwolves advance with a 103-96 win in Game 5 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768058 |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On March 21, 2026, Kleber was assigned to the [[South Bay Lakers]] to practice after missing six straight games with a back strain.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers big man sent to G League, but return could be soon |url=https://basketnews.com/news-243483-maxi-kleber-injury-update-back-strain-g-league-practice.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:EuroBasket Qualifier Austria vs Germany, 13 August 2014 - 094.JPG|thumb|Kleber with the German national team in 2014]]
Kleber has also played games for the senior [[Germany men's national basketball team|German national team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maxi Kleber International Stats|publisher=Basketball-Reference.com|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/maxi-kleber-1.html|accessdate=21 October 2020}}</ref> In 2014, he played for the team during the [[EuroBasket 2015 qualification|EuroBasket qualification rounds]]. Kleber was forced to sit out the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] as he was recovering from an Achilles injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watts |first=Tyler |date=25 July 2021 |title=Dallas Mavericks: Olympic basketball Day 1 recap: Josh Green's debut and more |url=https://thesmokingcuban.com/2021/07/25/mavericks-olympic-day-1-recap-josh-green/ |access-date=10 November 2024 |website=thesmokingcuban.com}}</ref>
